newsitem.title: USA: White House chides Congress on disaster bill.
newsitem.headline: White House chides Congress on disaster bill.

text.p: The White House said Friday President Clinton will veto a disaster relief bill and warned Republican congressional leaders to drop unacceptable conditions from the measure or face future vetoes.
Congress Thursday gave its final approval to an emergency $8.6 billion disaster aid bill.

Clinton refused to sign the bill because in addition to providing aid to 35 states hit by weather disasters, it also sets conditions on future federal budget negotiations and revises census procedures that critics say will underestimate minorities.
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry urged Congress to "send it to the president without any delay so the president can veto it and send it back."
Asked about comment by Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott that Congress would continue passing the same bill if Clinton vetoes it, McCurry said, "It borders on being ridiculous."
"People beat their heads against brick walls all the time," McCurry said. "They usually don't run major institutions of democracy."
